claims.text: The target high-entropy alloys span varying compositions.
Integrating machine learning with first-principles calculations will improve the accuracy of melting-temperature predictions relative to current methods.
Integrating machine learning with first-principles calculations will make melting-temperature prediction more computationally efficient.
The integrated approach will improve prediction of melting properties other than melting temperature.
The approach will be applicable across a wide range of high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The approach will be applicable across a wide range of high-entropy-alloy structures.
Improved predictive models of thermodynamic properties mediate the effect of the integrated approach.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn patterns from data generated by first-principles calculations.
Learning patterns from first-principles data produces more accurate melting-property predictions.
Accurate melting-property predictions can be obtained without explicitly accounting for phonon effects.
The integrated approach can provide accurate predictions without extensive experimental validation.
The approach is limited to high-entropy alloys.
The approach is limited to melting properties.
The approach may not generalize to other material classes or properties.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on training-data quality.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on training-data quantity.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on the machine-learning algorithm used.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on the first-principles calculation method used.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says accurate prediction can avoid explicit phonon effects, whereas cited record PMC6093928 states that failure to include explicit phonon effects limits phase-transition-temperature accuracy in CoCrFeMnNi.
